metadata.title: World SAMOSA Day l Delhi Samosa Trail l Japani, Matar, Moong Dal, Afghani, Mutton, Aloo, BBQ & more
metadata.description:
World Samosa Day is celebrated on September 5th, and on its eve, we set out on a dedicated Samosa Trail across Delhi, exploring the many forms, flavours, and philosophies behind this much-loved snack.

Our journey begins in the historic lanes of Chandni Chowk at Manohar Dhaba, home to the legendary Japani Samosa. Unlike the usual triangular form, this samosa stands out for its multi-layered, ultra-flaky pastry, fried to a delicate crisp. Each bite shatters into thin layers, revealing a mildly spiced filling, and is best enjoyed with their robust chole, making it a complete, deeply satisfying plate.

Next, we head to Kinari Bazar, where Sohan Sweets and Radhey Lal Halwai have been serving their matar samosa round the year. These samosas are all about comfort, soft, well-seasoned green peas filling, balanced spices, and a crust that’s crisp yet not heavy. Simple, honest, and immensely flavourful, this is the kind of samosa that keeps patrons coming back across generations.

In Paharganj, Janta Sweets offers a refreshing variation with their moong dal samosa. Lightly spiced and gently aromatic, the filling allows the natural nuttiness of the lentils to shine. What makes it especially interesting is the accompaniment, a warm, mildly spiced sabzi that turns the samosa into a fun snack..

The trail then moves west to Janakpuri, where Samosa Party brings a contemporary twist to tradition. Here, samosas take on playful, experimental avatars, from pizza-inspired fillings to BBQ-flavoured creations. Crisp on the outside and indulgent within, these fusion samosas showcase a mind-boggling variety while still retaining the soul of the classic samosa.

We conclude in Pitampura at the iconic Tilak Munjal, known for their large, generously filled samosas. The samosa is filled with a flavoursome potato filling and is served alongside chole and their signature imli chutney, which adds a sharp, tangy contrast. Hearty and indulgent, this is a samosa that truly eats like a meal.

From old-world halwai to modern-day innovators, this Samosa Trail captures Delhi’s enduring love for the samosa, across generations.
